tokens.name: plate
tokens.usage: Pressed-tin plate fill: the HUD gauge plate, spell slots, rail head, status chips, enemy name pills, the pause shell, dialogs, hint bars, spec bands and the loading screen. The fill is always 100% opaque so floor contrast stays computable; a whole widget may fade for show/hide and Reduce Motion, its fill never.

tokens.name: plate-raised
tokens.usage: Hovered list rows, inactive tabs, attribute cards and detail panes inside a plate. Every text token holds 4.5:1 on it (text 10.7:1, text-muted 7.1:1, text-disabled 5.1:1; 10:1 and up in High Contrast). Selected is enamel, not plate-raised.

tokens.name: well
tokens.usage: Sunk bar tracks, spell-slot wells (64 x 64), Spell Point sockets and the empty part of every meter. Every resource fill clears 5:1 on it.

tokens.name: lip
tokens.usage: The 2 px lip around every well: 3.45:1 on plate and 4.74:1 on well, so the full extent of a bar always reads. Also empty tally dots, empty pips and empty token rings on plate. In High Contrast it is white like enamel, so on enamel draw empties in ink-muted.

tokens.name: rim
tokens.usage: Printed cream rim, the inner 2 px edge on the top and left of every plate (10.1:1 on plate). With the ink outline it is the dual edge: on any floor one of the two clears 3:1 (ink on light floors, rim on dark ones). Also the light-string core (--tt-string-light-core) and .tt-divider at 50%.

tokens.name: rim-shade
tokens.usage: The same rim on the bottom and right edges of a plate, so the tin reads pressed. Decorative; never the only edge. White in High Contrast, so sunk, pressed and unlit pieces keep their full outline there.

tokens.name: ink
tokens.usage: The 3 px outer outline on every world-facing element (4 px in High Contrast), the hard print shadow, the 2 px keyline outside the focus ring, and all text on enamel and on coloured fills (16.8:1 on enamel).

tokens.name: enamel
tokens.usage: Light enamel ground: Tally tickets and tags, keycap faces, the interact prompt, item cards, dialogs' primary button, the .tt-empty tag, and Selected everywhere (tabs, filter chips, categories, plate cards; with the focus ring on top when focused). Always inside a 3 px ink outline because it nearly matches light floors.

tokens.name: enamel-shade
tokens.usage: Bands and footers on enamel, the keycap's lower lip, the grommet ring and a pressed keycap. ink holds 14:1 and ink-muted 5.7:1 on it.

tokens.name: veil
tokens.usage: Backdrop over the frozen world (drawn as a diorama stand-in, never a flat grid, never blurred) for the pause menu, dialogs and options. Text never sits on the veil itself, only on a plate or tag.

tokens.name: veil-death
tokens.usage: The lighter backdrop of the death screen, so the world (still running: death does not pause) stays visible behind the record. Text sits on the death plate, never on the veil.

tokens.name: text
tokens.usage: Primary text on plate (12.3:1), plate-raised (10.7:1) and well (16.9:1). Lit rank strokes on plate. Also the Physical damage number.

tokens.name: text-muted
tokens.usage: Secondary text on plate (8.1:1) and plate-raised (7.1:1): row labels (HP, ST, SP), inactive tab labels, hint labels, spec-band notes, the [I] Inventory reminder.

tokens.name: text-disabled
tokens.usage: Disabled labels on plate (5.9:1) and plate-raised (5.1:1), such as Allocate at 0 points and locked feats. Always paired with the lock glyph or a dashed edge.

tokens.name: ink-muted
tokens.usage: Secondary text on enamel (6.8:1) and enamel-shade (5.7:1): the Tally's remark line, cause lines, ticket footers. Empty tally dots and empty pips on enamel.

tokens.name: focus
tokens.usage: Keyboard and gamepad focus: a 3 px ring right outside the piece's own ink outline, with a 2 px ink keyline outside the ring (ink | focus | ink), so it reads on every ground: 13.0:1 on plate (yellow 19.6:1 in High Contrast); on light floors, where the ring alone is 1.1-1.3:1, the ink keyline carries it (14:1 and up). White is a hue no game signal uses, so focus never vanishes on a gold, red or green row.

tokens.name: vital
tokens.usage: Player Health fill (6.8:1 on well) and the low-health edge frame: an 8 px opaque band with a 3 px ink inner line at 25% Health or below, not pulsing (it is a frame, not a plate). A rose red kept apart from danger in hue and lightness.

tokens.name: vital-trail
tokens.usage: The damage-trail ghost on player, enemy and boss health bars (14.3:1 on well). Timing: Motion DamageTrail. In High Contrast it is cream, not white, so the ghost's top and bottom edges stay apart from the white lip.

tokens.name: heal
tokens.usage: Healing lead segment on the Health bar (timing: Motion HealLead) and '+N' heal numbers (11.6:1 on its ink outline).

tokens.name: stamina-green
tokens.usage: Stamina Green tier fill (66% and up, x1.25) and its pill ground with ink text (8.9:1).

tokens.name: stamina-yellow
tokens.usage: Stamina Yellow tier fill (33-66%, x1.0) and its pill ground with ink text (13.3:1). A lemon, kept off the reward gold.

tokens.name: danger
tokens.usage: Danger as a FILL, for threat only: the stamina Red tier (with ink stripes), the Exhausted debt hatch (StaminaDebtBar), enemy and boss health, error bands, the Drawback hatch. Ink text on it holds 6.0:1. Never small text on plate (use danger-text) and never player posture.

tokens.name: danger-text
tokens.usage: Danger as TEXT on plate (6.1:1) and plate-raised (5.3:1): 'Parry Failed!', the low-health HP number, error messages, the Drawback label, debuff chip rims.

tokens.name: delta-up
tokens.usage: Item compare: a stat that improves, as a pill fill with ink text and the arrow-up glyph. An alias of heal, so compare never borrows a stamina tier's meaning.

tokens.name: delta-down
tokens.usage: Item compare: a stat that gets worse, as a pill fill with ink text (6.0:1) and the arrow-down glyph.

tokens.name: stamina-red
tokens.usage: Stamina Red tier (above 0, below 33%, x0.75). An alias of danger so the warning reads as one family; told apart from Health by hue, row and the ink stripes.

tokens.name: foe
tokens.usage: Enemy and boss health fill. One colour at every health level; low health shows by the trail and the 25% notch, not a hue shift.

tokens.name: posture
tokens.usage: Player and enemy posture bars (10.1:1 on well). A neutral pewter for steadiness, so it never competes with the stamina tier colours beside it. Player posture broken = this fill with an ink hatch and the rim turned to rim: no red, no chip (the player has no posture-break logic yet, TODO(DECISION)).

tokens.name: spell-points
tokens.usage: Spell Point tokens (a row designed for 10-16 tokens in the 268 px track; 13 at default INT) and the SP cost dots on spell slots (6.8:1 on well).

tokens.name: good
tokens.usage: Reward gold, one meaning (worth having): positive callouts, reward stamps, Elite tier diamonds, rarity Gold. As text on plate 8.1:1. Never lit rank strokes (those are text on plate, ink on enamel): a gold full bundle means rarity Gold only.

tokens.name: rarity-common
tokens.usage: Common item names on plate (9.0:1) and plate-raised (7.9:1). Badge: an empty ring.

tokens.name: rarity-green
tokens.usage: Green item names (6.4:1 on plate-raised) and the Green band with ink text. Badge: 1 tally stroke.

tokens.name: rarity-blue
tokens.usage: Blue item names (5.4:1 on plate-raised). Badge: 2 strokes.

tokens.name: rarity-purple
tokens.usage: Purple item names (5.2:1 on plate-raised). Badge: 3 strokes. Blue and Purple converge for deuteranopes: the stroke count and the colour word carry them.

tokens.name: rarity-red
tokens.usage: Red item names (5.0:1 on plate-raised). Badge: 4 strokes. Shares a family with danger-text; the badge and the word 'Red' keep them apart.

tokens.name: rarity-gold
tokens.usage: Gold item names and band (7.0:1 on plate-raised). Badge: the full bundle (four strokes and the slash). The full bundle in gold means rarity Gold and nothing else.

tokens.name: feat-common
tokens.usage: Common feat badge (circle) and tier word: 10.0:1 on plate.

tokens.name: feat-rare
tokens.usage: Rare feat badge (a flat-top hexagon, everywhere) and tier word: 7.2:1 on plate. Its own hue, so feat tiers never borrow item rarity colours.

tokens.name: feat-legendary
tokens.usage: Legendary feat badge (eight-point starburst) and tier word: 5.62:1 on plate and 4.88:1 on plate-raised (both clear 4.5:1, so plate-raised is allowed; 9.5:1 and up in High Contrast). Magenta, so 'Gold' never means both a Legendary feat and a Gold item.

tokens.name: buff
tokens.usage: Buff status chip rim (8.2:1 on plate). Buff chips also carry a raised notch on top.

tokens.name: debuff
tokens.usage: Debuff status chip rim (6.1:1 on plate). Debuff chips also carry a pinked, sawtooth bottom edge.

tokens.name: dmg-physical
tokens.usage: Physical, Slash, Pierce and Blunt damage numbers, inside a 3 px ink outline (17.5:1). No type glyph: only non-Physical numbers carry one. Whether busy melee fights need the subtype on the number is TODO(DECISION) in DamageNumber.

tokens.name: dmg-fire
tokens.usage: Fire damage numbers and the flame glyph (7.9:1 on the ink outline).

tokens.name: dmg-frost
tokens.usage: Frost damage numbers and the six-armed snowflake glyph (13.4:1 on ink).

tokens.name: dmg-lightning
tokens.usage: Lightning damage numbers and the bolt glyph (14.6:1 on ink).

tokens.name: dmg-poison
tokens.usage: Poison damage numbers and the droplet glyph (12.4:1 on ink).

tokens.name: dmg-corrosive
tokens.usage: Corrosive damage numbers and the corrosive glyph, a drop falling into a basin (11.6:1 on ink).

tokens.name: dmg-arcane
tokens.usage: Arcane damage numbers and the four-point sparkle glyph (8.4:1 on ink).

tokens.name: dmg-shadow
tokens.usage: Shadow (Curse) numbers print INVERTED: this dark fill inside a dmg-shadow-edge outline, then the ink outline, plus the spiral glyph. Its silhouette is unlike any other number.

tokens.name: dmg-shadow-edge
tokens.usage: The light outline of an inverted Shadow number (11.8:1 against dmg-shadow), itself inside the ink outline so it holds on light floors.

tokens.name: dmg-radiant
tokens.usage: Radiant (Holy) numbers with an inner 2 px good halo inside the ink outline and the sun-ray glyph (16.1:1 on ink).

tokens.name: biome-verdant
tokens.usage: Map tile and title-card swatch for the Verdant Wilds. Fills only, never under text.

tokens.name: biome-searing
tokens.usage: Map tile and title-card swatch for the Searing Expanse. Fills only.

tokens.name: biome-mire
tokens.usage: Map tile and title-card swatch for the Mire of Echoes. Fills only.

tokens.name: biome-crystal
tokens.usage: Map tile and title-card swatch for the Crystal Caverns. Fills only.

tokens.name: biome-storm
tokens.usage: Map tile and title-card swatch for the Storm Peaks. Fills only.

tokens.name: biome-withered
tokens.usage: Map tile and title-card swatch for the Withered Kingdom. Fills only.

tokens.name: world-blockout
tokens.usage: Scenery stand-in: the light grey dev blockout floor (.tt-floor-blockout, .tt-diorama--blockout). The hardest ground for light edges (white focus is 1.28:1 on it), so HUD previews always show it. Theme-invariant: level art, which High Contrast never restyles. Never a UI colour, never under text.

tokens.name: world-blockout-line
tokens.usage: Scenery stand-in: the 2 px grid lines of the blockout floor, every 96 px. Theme-invariant.

tokens.name: world-grass
tokens.usage: Scenery stand-in: the grass floor (.tt-floor-grass, .tt-diorama--grass) and tree canopies. Theme-invariant.

tokens.name: world-grass-dot
tokens.usage: Scenery stand-in: the grass floor's dots and the darker checker tile. Theme-invariant.

tokens.name: world-sand
tokens.usage: Scenery stand-in: the sand floor (.tt-floor-sand, .tt-diorama--sand), paths and patches. Theme-invariant.

tokens.name: world-sand-dot
tokens.usage: Scenery stand-in: the sand floor's dots and darker checker tile. Theme-invariant.

tokens.name: world-mire
tokens.usage: Scenery stand-in: the mire floor (.tt-floor-mire, .tt-diorama--mire), a mid-dark ground where neither ink nor a thin dark line holds. Theme-invariant.

tokens.name: world-mire-dot
tokens.usage: Scenery stand-in: the mire floor's dots and lighter checker tile. Theme-invariant.

tokens.name: world-night
tokens.usage: Scenery stand-in: the night floor (.tt-floor-night, .tt-diorama--night), where the ink outline vanishes (1.2:1) and the rim carries the edge. Also dark level art: plinths, slots, the display case. Theme-invariant.

tokens.name: world-night-dot
tokens.usage: Scenery stand-in: the night floor's dots and lighter checker tile. Theme-invariant.

tokens.name: world-snow
tokens.usage: Scenery stand-in: the snow floor (.tt-floor-snow, .tt-diorama--snow), the lightest ground (white focus 1.10:1; the ink keyline carries focus here). Also highlights on level art. Theme-invariant.

tokens.name: world-snow-dot
tokens.usage: Scenery stand-in: the snow floor's dots and darker checker tile. Theme-invariant.

tokens.name: world-light
tokens.usage: Alias for light level art drawn in previews (thumbnails, relic faces, prop highlights), so components never write floor hex values. Theme-invariant.

tokens.name: world-dark
tokens.usage: Alias for dark level art drawn in previews (plinths, slots, prop outlines, the front-end display case). Theme-invariant.

tokens.name: world-shade
tokens.usage: Scenery stand-in: flat contact shadows under diorama props (a hard ellipse, never a blur). Theme-invariant; never a UI print shadow (that is ink at opacity-print).

groups.name: Tally voice
groups.note: Rowdies: the counting machine's stamped lettering. Celebration, callouts, tickets, the wordmark. Sizes are design px at 1920x1080; UMG points = px x 0.75.

styles.name: tally-display
styles.usage: The wordmark on the title and loading screens. Cased with ToUpper at display time.

styles.name: tally-title
styles.usage: Plate titles (feat, technique, level), the level number, expedition card titles.

styles.name: tally-heading
styles.usage: The 'Paused' nameplate, dialog titles, service screen headers.

styles.name: callout
styles.usage: Combat callouts under the player, letters only with a 4 px ink outline.

styles.name: kicker
styles.usage: Ticket and plate kickers, cased with ToUpper. The only caps the Tally uses.

styles.name: pop
styles.usage: Floating damage numbers (crits at 45 px). Proportional digits are fine: pops never tick in place.

groups.name: World voice
groups.note: Atkinson Hyperlegible Next ExtraBold, tracked caps: the serious register for death, biomes, bosses and endings. No ornament, no remarks.

styles.name: world-title
styles.usage: Death screen headline, ending titles. Cased with ToUpper; the TextBlock keeps 'You Died'.

styles.name: world-heading
styles.usage: Biome title cards, boss names on the boss bar and boss intro banner.

groups.name: Interface
groups.note: Atkinson Hyperlegible Next, built for low-vision legibility. Nothing below 20 px (13.3 px at 720p).

styles.name: ui-title
styles.usage: Tab labels, item names, ticket main lines, list headers, the pickup prompt.

styles.name: ui-body
styles.sample: A faintly humming amulet. The Mage Tower can identify it.
styles.usage: Descriptions, menu rows, dialog bodies, tooltips.

styles.name: ui-label
styles.usage: The floor size: status names, hints, remarks, footers, row labels.

groups.name: Numerals
groups.note: Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono: every digit is 0.632 em wide by default, so live numbers never shift in Slate (which ignores OpenType tnum). Size each box for its longest value.

styles.name: num-xl
styles.usage: Death countdown, the Skill Points token.

styles.name: num-s
styles.usage: Status durations, stack counts, ledger counts, keycap letters (at 800).

tokens.name: space-1
tokens.usage: Glyph to label inside chips and keycaps.

tokens.name: space-2
tokens.usage: Gap between stacked tickets, between chips, row inner padding.

tokens.name: space-3
tokens.usage: Bar to bar inside the gauge plate; button inner padding.

tokens.name: space-4
tokens.usage: Plate inner padding on the HUD.

tokens.name: space-5
tokens.usage: Plate inner padding in menus; gap between menu columns.

tokens.name: space-6
tokens.usage: The HUD edge margin at 1920x1080.

tokens.name: space-7
tokens.usage: Gap between a HUD cluster and the next; minimum mouse target.

tokens.name: space-8
tokens.usage: The TV-safe HUD margin option.

tokens.name: radius-key
tokens.usage: Keyboard keycaps and small square sockets.

tokens.name: radius-tag
tokens.usage: Tickets, tags, item cards, tooltips.

tokens.name: radius-plate
tokens.usage: Every plate: gauge plate, spell slots, menu shell, dialogs.

tokens.name: radius-pill
tokens.usage: Chips, multiplier pills, gamepad shoulder keycaps. Pills only; never a card.

shadow.note: Hard print offsets only: no blur, no glow, no glass.

tokens.name: print-hud
tokens.usage: Under HUD plates and tags, below the ink outline.

tokens.name: print-menu
tokens.usage: Under the pause shell, dialogs and hanging menu tags.

tokens.name: print-pressed
tokens.usage: A pressed keycap or button: the shadow collapses as the face sinks 3 px.

tokens.name: stroke-outline
tokens.usage: Outer ink outline on every world-facing element: plates, tags, keycaps, bars over the world, damage numbers. Callout letters use 4 px.

tokens.name: stroke-outline-hc
tokens.usage: Outer outline in the High Contrast theme.

tokens.name: stroke-rim
tokens.usage: The inner printed rim of a plate and the lip around a well.

tokens.name: stroke-focus
tokens.usage: The focus ring: 3 px, drawn right outside the piece's own ink outline (offset = the outline width), with a 2 px ink keyline outside it.

tokens.name: opacity-print
tokens.usage: Print shadow strength on the HUD.

tokens.name: opacity-unaffordable
tokens.usage: A spell icon the player cannot afford, always with hollow cost dots. An icon only: plate fills are never below 100%.
